sentences.text:
Satguru Traders vs State Through Food Inspector on 30 July,
2021

Author: Vinod Chatterji Koul
Bench: Vinod Chatterji Koul

Sr. No. 210
 High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh

At Jammu
 Crta No. 33/2015
 Ia No. 01/2015
Satguru Traders ...
Petitioner/Appellant(s)

Through: Mr. Sanjay Sharma, Advocate.
 v/s
 State through Food Inspector, Ramban .... Respondent(s)
 Through: None.

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vinod Chatterji Koul, Judge
 Order

1. The applicant has filed this application seeking transfer of criminal complaint pending before the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramban under Section 7(i) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i)
of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to the court of competent jurisdiction at Rajouri.

entities.text: court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramban
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The transfer of the case has been sought primarily on the ground that the applicant- Chander Kanta is an old aged lady of more than 85 years old and also not in good health.

3. Respondent has filed objections and resisted the transfer of the case on the ground that transfer of the case would cause inconvenience to the witnesses and trial of the case is to be conducted in a court within the jurisdiction of which cause has arisen.
4. I have gone through the grounds taken in the applications and submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant.

I do not find any sufficient ground warranting transfer of this case from the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramban that would cause inconvenience not only to the complaint but also to the witnesses which are yet to be examined in this case.

While dismissing the petition seeking transfer, it is observed that in case the petitioner makes an application before the trial court with sufficient reasons shown, the trial court shall consider the same in accordance with law.
6. The petition shall stand dismissed.
7. The petitioner shall appear before the trial court.
8. Interim direction, if any, shall stand vacated.
9. Order be communicated to the trial court.

opennyai_summary.facts:
1. The applicant has filed this application seeking transfer of criminal complaint pending before the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramban under Section 7(i) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i)
of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to the court of competent jurisdiction at Rajouri.
2. The transfer of the case has been sought primarily on the ground that the applicant- Chander Kanta is an old aged lady of more than 85 years old and also not in good health.
3. Respondent has filed objections and resisted the transfer of the case on the ground that transfer of the case would cause inconvenience to the witnesses and trial of the case is to be conducted in a court within the jurisdiction of which cause has arisen.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS: I do not find any sufficient ground warranting transfer of this case from the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramban that would cause inconvenience not only to the complaint but also to the witnesses which are yet to be examined in this case.
opennyai_summary.decision:
At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he would be satisfied if trial court is asked to consider his application for exemption whenever sufficient ground is shown.
While dismissing the petition seeking transfer, it is observed that in case the petitioner makes an application before the trial court with sufficient reasons shown, the trial court shall consider the same in accordance with law.
6. The petition shall stand dismissed.
7. The petitioner shall appear before the trial court.
8. Interim direction, if any, shall stand vacated.
9. Order be communicated to the trial court.
